description.value: Walk-in tent camping in grassy meadows along 7 km of rocky Salt Spring Island shoreline, with sweeping views over Swanson Channel and strong wildlife watching; potable water is shut down November 1–March 15 and all sites require carrying gear from the parking lot.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: OSM tags provide explicit confirmation of walk-in tent camping (caravans=no, tents=yes, shower=no, drinking_water=yes, toilets=yes, power_supply=no). The website corroborates the walk-in nature of the campground and confirms reservations are accepted via camping.bcparks.ca; it also notes the drinking water system is shut down seasonally (Nov 1–Mar 15). The 'Walk-in Camping' designation in the park name is direct evidence that campsites are accessible only on foot or by bicycle, not by vehicle.
concerns: OSM community field lists 'Sidney' but the park is located on Salt Spring Island — this appears to be a geographic categorization error.
No address or direct phone number in the OSM record; contact is through the BC Parks general line only.
Drinking water is shut down seasonally Nov 1–Mar 15; off-season cyclists should plan accordingly.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Ruckle Park's walk-in campground is an excellent fit for the WWC directory — it is a scenic, vehicle-free BC Parks campsite on Salt Spring Island directly suited to touring cyclists arriving by ferry or bike, with drinking water, toilets, and reservations available.

wow_evidence: Walk-in Camping designation... accessible only on foot or by bicycle, not by vehicle
